title: Mount Athos
hookLine: a peninsula of monasteries given over to prayer

lines: A FINGER OF LAND IN GREECE.
cards: Well before sunrise, a monk walks slowly around a stone courtyard carrying a long wooden board, striking it with a mallet, a rhythm that carries over the walls and down the cliffs to the sea. It's the call to prayer.

This is Mount Athos, a mountain at the tip of a long finger of land in northern Greece, given over to monasteries. Watchfulness, the prayer rope and the Jesus Prayer are daily work here. Today's word: Mount Athos.

teach.b: The monks call it the Holy Mountain, in Greek Hagion Oros: a whole peninsula of monasteries, small monastic villages, and hermits' huts clinging to the rocks above the water.

There's a story the monks tell about how it began. Tradition says Mary, the mother of Jesus, was at sea when a storm drove her ship off course; she came ashore here, loved the place, and asked her Son to give it to her.

teach.h: THE GARDEN OF THE MOTHER OF GOD.
teach.b: So Athos is called the Garden of the Mother of God, and the monks speak of her as its abbess, its true head. Why a mountain?
Luke gives one picture of Jesus at prayer: "he went out into a mountain to pray, and continued all night in prayer to God." The monks take that night of prayer as a pattern.

Before great feasts they keep vigils that run through the night, with candles, chant, and the lamps before the icons set gently swinging as the feast comes to its height. And here's the part worth carrying home.
The monks don't describe themselves as escaping the world.

They speak of praying for it: for people who never pray, for people who will never learn their names, for the whole world. So somewhere on a cliff above the sea, someone may be praying for you, and will never meet you.
The psalmist looked at the hills, asked where help comes from, and answered himself: "My help cometh from the LORD, which made heaven and earth."

how: Orthodox monks on Mount Athos keep a daily round of services, private prayer and work, with long vigils before feasts; Orthodox Christians and other visitors go there on pilgrimage.

the peak in Sinai where Moses received the law

games.q: you're a pilgrim at a monastery gate on Athos, before dawn. a monk walks past striking a long wooden board. what's happening?
o: a work crew is starting on the walls.
it's a warning that the gate is closing.
games.why: the knocking board calls the monks to prayer while it's still dark. the day on the Holy Mountain starts in church.

practice: Close your eyes and picture it: stone walls on a cliff, a wooden board knocking, lamps lit in a dark church, and below, the sea going from black to gray to silver. Stand quietly at the back; you don't have to say anything.
If you pray, join their prayer for the world by naming one person far away from you; if you don't, simply hold that person in mind while the light comes up.

wordCard.voice: Mount Athos. The Holy Mountain: a peninsula of monasteries in Greece, given over to prayer for the world.

orig.note: Greek: the Holy Mountain, the name the monks use for Athos.

carryVoice: Your line: the holy mountain. On a cliff above the sea, the world is being prayed for. That's today, done.
